answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs thus has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the raven hash is checked against the sonnet checkpoint at intake, the cipher audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 15 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
